sourceFlowReconstruction: L1-7 Mishnah: seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is separated from his house to the Parhedrin chamber; another kohen is prepared in his stead lest a disqualification befall him. R. Yehuda: another wife is also prepared lest his wife die, as it says 'vekhiper ba'ado uve'ad beito', beito zo ishto. They said to him: if so, there is no end to the matter.

L8-11 Gemara cites 'tenan hatam': seven days before the burning of the parah they would separate the kohen who burns it from his house to the chamber on the face of the Bira, north-east; it was called Lishkat Beit HaEven.
L12-14: why that name? because all its acts (Rashi: the parah's) were with dung, stone and earth vessels.

L14-20: mai ta'ama? since a tevul yom is fit for the parah, as taught (ditnan): they would make the kohen who burns the parah tamei and immerse him, to remove from the hearts of the Sadducees, who said it was done by me'orvei shemesh; the Rabbis instituted dung/stone/earth vessels, which do not receive tumah, so that it not be treated lightly.
L20-24: why north-east? since it is a chatat and a chatat requires north, and of it is written 'el nokhach penei ohel moed', the Rabbis instituted a north-east chamber so that it have a heker.

L24-27: mai bira? Rabba bar bar Chana in the name of R. Yochanan: a place on the Temple Mount named Bira. Reish Lakish: the whole Mikdash is called Bira, as it says 'habira asher hakhinoti'. No decision.

L27-31: mena hanei milei? R. Minyomi bar Chilkiya - R. Machseya bar Idi - R. Yochanan: 'ka'asher asah bayom hazeh tzivah Hashem la'asot lekhaper aleikhem': la'asot = acts of the parah, lekhaper = acts of Yom Kippur.
L32-34: granted the whole verse cannot be about the parah (lekhaper is written and the parah is not for atonement), but say the whole verse is about Yom Kippur?
L34-38: amri: yalif tzivah tzivah; here 'tzivah Hashem la'asot', there 'zot chukat hatorah asher tzivah Hashem lemor'; as there parah so here parah; as here perisha so there perisha.
L39: 've'eima' - a further challenge begins; the page ends with nothing after it. The derivation is therefore still open at the physical end of 2a.

dafLevelDefects.fieldSays: When the same word or phrase appears in two Torah passages, the rules of one passage carry over to the other.
dafLevelDefects.sourceSupports: The page has one instance only: 'yalif tzivah tzivah', linking 'tzivah Hashem la'asot' to 'asher tzivah Hashem lemor' (there parah so here parah; here perisha so there perisha). The term gezerah shavah, 'or phrase', and a general carry-over rule are not on the daf or in its Rashi. A daf-level field may rest only on lines of this daf; the entry restates a single case as a general rule of how the Talmud works.

dafLevelDefects.fieldSays: Because a tvul yom is fit for the Red Heifer, they would deliberately make the kohen who burns it tamei and immerse him, to refute the Sadducees...
dafLevelDefects.sourceSupports: On the page 'keivan ditvul yom kasher bapara' is the reason for the vessel enactment (answer to mai ta'ama), and the Mishnah 'metam'in hayu' is cited (ditnan) as support that a tevul yom is fit; the only purpose stated for making him tamei is 'lehotzi milibban shel tzedukin'. The entry moves the page's reason to a different clause. Confidence: moderate (lower severity than the first).
